newsitem.title: FRANCE: French want old politicians retired.
newsitem.headline: French want old politicians retired.

text.p: A vast majority of French citizens wants politicians aged over 75 barred from seeking election, according to a poll released on Friday.
The survey, for the weekly Le Figaro Magazine by the Sofres group, showed 82 percent of 1,000 people polled would agree with legislation preventing people aged over 75 from standing for parliament.

No such legislation is in the works but aides to Prime Minister Alain Juppe recently indicated he would like the oldest members of his own centre-right coalition not to stand again in general elections in 1998.

The oldest member of the National Assembly, centre-rightist Charles Ehrmann, 85, said he had no intention of withdrawing and opinion polls showed he was favourite to retain his seat. There are 20 people aged over 75 in France's 577-seat parliament.

The same poll showed 58 percent of the public believed that extreme rightist Jean-Marie Le Pen's National Front (NF) party should be represented in parliament on grounds it should be allowed to be heard like other political parties.
The figure was eight percent higher than that found in a similar poll a month earlier.

Although credited with the backing of about 15 percent of voters, the NF has no seats in parliament because it has so far been unable to make deals with other parties in France's complicated first-past-the-post system voting system.
